parakeet: Number two, megachurch pastors are narcissists. But let me explain. When I say mega church pastors are narcissists, I'm not saying that every megachurch pastor has narcissistic personality disorder. I'm saying mega church culture naturally rewards and reproduces narcissistic traits. Grandiosity, admiration dependency, image management, low accountability, spiritualized authority, and the belief that one person's vision represents the highest good. And in many ways, this is built into the theology. When a religious culture reveres an all-powerful being who demands worship, obedience, surrender, loyalty, and constant praise, it should not surprise us when the visible leader begins to mirror those same traits. The pastor becomes the human reflection of the authority figure the community already worships. But the congregation is not passive in this. Members often crave a leader who mirrors that God complex. They want someone chosen, certain, powerful, anointed, untouchable, and larger than life. So they don't just tolerate the persona, they help create it. Megachurch pastors often carry a complex abandonment wound shaped by two realities. First, they're constantly preaching about a God who is supposed to be active, but they have to live with God's absence in real time. Prayers go unanswered, people don't get healed, families fall apart, and members leave. Second, because the church is built around their persona, they often experience rejection from members as personal abandonment. People leave the church, question the vision, criticize the leader, or stop giving, and the pastor feels betrayed by the very people they believe they were called to serve. So the pastor builds a persona to protect against that abandonment and rejection. The persona becomes bigger, stronger, more certain, more anointed, more untouchable. And the more the pastor performs that authority, the more they resemble the divine authority figure the culture already reveres. So then, when narcissistic traits show up, the church calls it leadership.
